proved_in_candidate: At a nonsingleton rank-zero anchor restoration, the terminal palette contains the banned color u and the mover q is outside the independent root.
If the attacked anchor a is absent from the terminal palette, that palette is exactly {u,c} and arbitrary-state restoration forces a into the mover palette Q(q).
The only alternate is r->a. If it is physically legal and unbanned, rank zero forces its successor R={a,c,q} to be nondominating.
In the shared-secondary branch, a missed witness of R is either u with uq a graph nonedge, or it forces a two-attack retained ladder ending in u in Q(w).

certified_control.sharp_boundary: Two rank-zero restoration rows share the dominating banned state {1,7,10}, which is absent from the literal greatest eternal family.
